data.description:
## Context / Problem
The Gerrit Verified gate takes 21-47 minutes end-to-end. Measured on run #1823 (id 30569775555), the critical path is a SINGLE job: `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` at 18.6m. Every other job is <=8m; if macOS vanished the run would finish in ~8m.

Worse, macOS runner concurrency is capped (peak 4 concurrent macOS jobs observed across 25 sampled jobs from the last 30 runs). When 6 changes were dispatched within 10 seconds, the later ones queued 6.7-8.4m for a macOS runner. That queue is what turns a 21m run into the 41-47m the operator observes. So macOS job DURATION is doubly valuable: it is both the critical path and the thing holding a scarce runner slot that other changes are waiting on.

Within that job, the `--cov` default-suite step is 15.4m of the 18.6m. The macOS cells pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, so coverage.py traces the entire run — but NOTHING consumes the macOS coverage number. The `fail_under = 70` floor in `[tool.coverage.report]` is enforced identically by the three ubuntu cells running the exact same test selection.

## Approach
Make the coverage flags conditional on the matrix OS in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: ubuntu cells keep `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, macOS cells run without them. This is a pure duplicate-work removal — the identical 7856 tests still execute on macOS, and the coverage floor is still gated three times over on ubuntu.

Rejected alternative: dropping the macOS cell entirely. That is the obvious 2x win and it is exactly the platform-compat coverage (flock/mkdir lock, gtimeout) the cell exists for. Out of bounds — the requirement is no coverage loss.

Rejected alternative: keeping `--cov` on macOS but adding `--cov-fail-under=0`. Pointless: it keeps the tracing cost, which IS the cost, and only removes an assertion that already passes.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — the `test` job default-suite step only. The integration-tier step already passes no `--cov` and is untouched. The `-n` worker counts, `--dist` modes, `--basetemp`, and every drift gate are untouched.
- `docs/coverage.md` — record that coverage is collected on the ubuntu cells only, and why.

Explicitly NOT in scope: sharding the macOS job, changing `-n`, and the verify-identity partial-clone fix (recorded separately on epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc). Those are separate changes with their own risk profiles.

## Testing
No new testable behavior — this is a CI workflow configuration change. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the substring `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (line 67), which this change preserves; the parity suite must stay green. Verification is observational: the next Verified run must show the macOS default-suite step faster with an unchanged pass count (7856 passed), and the ubuntu cells must still print the coverage report and enforce the floor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The macOS matrix cells run the default suite with no `--cov*` flags.
- The ubuntu matrix cells still pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered` and still enforce `fail_under = 70`.
- The set of tests executed on macOS is unchanged (same `-m` selection; 7856 passed, 76-77 skipped).
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes unchanged.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- `docs/coverage.md` states that coverage is collected on ubuntu cells only.
data.title: Drop coverage collection from the macOS pytest cells (CI wall-clock)
